note: Shared parity contract for the PPG pulse gate. BOTH tools/test_protocol.py AND app/test/ppg_test.dart build these inputs from this spec and assert the same expected verdict. If the two implementations ever drift, one suite fails.

synthetic.formula: floor(dc * (1 + ac_fraction * (sin(p) + harmonic_fraction*sin(2p)))) where p = 2*pi*(bpm/60)*i/rate_hz. floor (not round) so Python and Dart agree exactly on ties.

cases.name: synthetic_48bpm
cases.why: a slow but genuine resting pulse must be accepted

cases.name: synthetic_95bpm
cases.why: an elevated rate must still be accepted

cases.name: real_capture
cases.why: the real 0x3A stream carries no pulse (PROTOCOL.md 6.2.3a)

cases.name: three_byte_misdecode
cases.why: genuinely periodic at an artificial 4-sample byte-alignment period; GUARD 1 must reject it rather than report 161 bpm

cases.name: monotonic_drift
cases.why: drift peaks nowhere; GUARD 2 must reject it rather than report 49 bpm

cases.name: flat_dc
cases.why: a perfectly flat trace has no excursion and no period

cases.name: pulse_behind_agc_transient
cases.why: a leading transient (the band's AGC settle) must not silence a real pulse — it wrecks the autocorrelation variance unless the signal is winsorized

cases.name: pulse_with_dropouts
cases.why: BLE dropouts arrive as zeros; they must not shift the apparent rate, and must not destroy the analysis either
